newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baer says some Swiss mid-caps are good 1997 buys.
newsitem.headline: Baer says some Swiss mid-caps are good 1997 buys.

text.p: Bank Julius Baer said Swiss mid-cap companies stood to benefit from several factors next year that will boost their performance on the Swiss stock market after being overshadowed by blue chips in 1996.

Baer's December Swiss research report named six mid-sized stocks as recommedations, meaning they meet selection criteria aimed at reducing economic risk that will remain in the sector of medium capitalised companies.
In addition to mid-caps, Baer said its 1997 investment favourites included some large companies which would continue to post double-digit earnings growth in the future.

"We expect banks and insurance companies to have considerable upside potential as beneficiaries of the current structural changes," it said about recent big reorganising steps in the financial sector.
The six favoured mid-caps included investment bank VP Bank Vaduz, speciality construction equipment maker Hilti and machinery and plant engineer Georg Fischer .
Baer upgraded Georg Fischer last month from underperform to outperform the Swiss Small and Middle Companies Index (SSMCI).
The other three were chemicals and pharma specialist Siegfried, construction and adhesives chemicals group Sika and Compagnie Financiere Michelin, the French tyremaker's Swiss holding company.
Baer said the Swiss stock market was dominated in 1996 by the shares of large groups, who had driven the year's bull run by focusing clearly on promising core business segements.
"In our view, the extent of the underperformance of the stock of numerous mid-cap companies seems to be unjustified," the bank wrote.
Baer said factors favouring mid-caps next year included their cyclical nature, which give them a better chance to profit from steady growth now expected in their major export markets.
Low interest rates and a weaker Swiss franc exchange rate against major export currencies would also help.
"Since these companies generally generate a high proportion of their sales in Europe, they could well be positively affected by the economic recovery which is expected there," Baer said.
Baer said the mid-caps it recommended met six criteria aimed at reducing risk from an unexpected shortfall in economic growth, currency turbulance or other factors.

The criteria include a free-float on the stock market of at least 200 million Swiss francs, earnings growth even if the economy remains sluggish, sound balance sheet ratios and an advantageous short and medium-term valuation.
